messages:
Maya: heads-up — CypressRidge just pinged with a pretty bad p99 regression on their tenant. Started ~09:15 UTC, they report p99 ~18s for /v1/generate (was ~4s). They provided a short repro and request ids.
Alex: thanks for the flag, reaching out to the customer now. Can we get metrics (p95/p99) and queue lengths?
Sam: looking at infra dashboards — I see a jump in queue depth for tenant=cypressridge around 09:12 UTC, concurrent inflight up x3, backend model latency also slightly up but not enough to explain 18s. Likely backlog at frontend queue.
Priya: can you paste the request ids? I want to correlate with rate-limiter + token-bucket logs.
Maya: here are two request ids they gave: req_0a3f4b and req_0a3f76. quick log snippet: ```
[09:14:58] request=req_0a3f4b tenant=cypressridge queued=true queue_pos=42 backpressure=true
[09:14:59] request=req_0a3f4b dispatched=true worker=gw-12 process_start=09:15:16
[09:15:16] worker=gw-12 start_infer model=gpt-open-7b-q4 seq_len=2048 tokens=512 infer_ms=1200
[09:15:34] request=req_0a3f4b completed status=200 latency=18320ms
```
Maya: queue_pos=42 — oof.
Sam: that aligns with a noisy-burst behavior — tenant sent bursts that exceeded token-bucket and queued behind other tenants. We have p99 skin due to queueing.
Priya: is this on shared hosted capacity? If so we can add a short-term reservation or priority lane (safelist) so their traffic bypasses soft backpressure while we investigate. Also can temporarily pin them to a less-bursty model variant or reduce max_concurrency.
Alex: customer asks for immediate relief, they'd accept a temporary priority lane for 2 hours while you triage.
Sam: I can add a temporary reservation. Running: ```/infra reserve-tenant --tenant=cypressridge --rps=10 --burst=40 --duration=2h --reason=\"support rescue\"```
ops-bot: reservation created id=rsv-97531 tenant=cypressridge rps=10 burst=40 expires=+2h status=active
Priya: added a temporary priority route that routes their requests to reserved slots and relaxes queueing. Also pinned their model to gpt-open-7b-q4-stable (no autoswitch).
Maya: after reservation, p99 dropped to ~4.5s within 30s — looks promising.
Sam: created an incident ticket INC-2026-7789 and linked to observability. I also raised a short alert tweak to fire earlier for per-tenant queue depth > 20.
Priya: root cause notes so far: sudden burst from tenant (likely batch job) causing frontend queue to pile. Model infer time contributed ~1.2s per request, but main delta was waiting in queue. Temporary mitigations: reservation (rsv-97531), pin model, reduced default concurrency for that tenant to 4.
Alex: I'll confirm with CypressRidge that latencies are back and ask them to identify what caused the burst. Suggest they throttle their batch job or use our bulk-embed endpoint with a reservation.
Maya: follow-ups: 1) Priya to propose a safer auto-safelist playbook (criteria + limits), 2) Sam to add long-term per-tenant token-bucket adjustments and a rolling window anomaly detector, 3) Alex to confirm customer and close when stable.
Priya: quick config snippet we applied: ```json
{"tenant":"cypressridge","reservation_id":"rsv-97531","rps":10,"burst":40,"pin_model":"gpt-open-7b-q4-stable","expires":"2026-03-17T11:15:00Z"}
```
Sam: FYI we'll keep reservation for 2h and then auto-drop. If customer still needs, escalate to dedicated capacity sales/SE.
Alex: customer confirmed improved performance and will pause the batch for now. I'll update the ticket and ask for a writeup. :thumbsup:
Maya: thanks team, closing thread once Alex confirms final sign-off.
